title: A Summer for the Postcard
premise: Rosalind Pemberton has spent a decade keeping her heart in careful training: writing romance under a pen name while living invisibly at her late grandfather's lighthouse, tending the orchard he left her. When a clerical error places Julian Ash—her first love, who vanished twenty years ago after a family scandal—on the same deed, the two are legally bound to co-manage the orchard for one summer before the county can repossess it. As grafting season forces them into daily proximity, old letters surface revealing her grandfather orchestrated their reunion, believing love is a debt worth collecting. At the summer's end auction, Rosalind must choose between selling the orchard to fund her escape and bidding everything—including her pen name's secret and her whole heart—to keep it, and Julian, alive.
about_author: Sable Amberdale is the pen name of a former lighthouse archivist who spent years cataloguing letters never sent, and it shows. She writes romances about people who mistake duty for destiny, from a cottage she refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A county clerk's letter arrives naming Julian Ash as co-heir to the orchard deed—a name Rosalind buried two decades ago. She storms the records office, finds the error is airtight, and learns the orchard faces repossession unless both heirs work it through the season. The emotional beat: dread sharpening into stubborn resolve, as the heart-muscle doctrine gets its first crack.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Rosalind and Julian. Julian arrives with a city suit and a guilty conscience, and the two wage polite war over pruning methods while the trees quietly outlast them. A shared storm-night repair of the orchard wall cracks the silence between them; Julian admits he left to protect her family from his father's ruin. The beat: tenderness disguised as argument.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Repairing the cellar wall, Julian uncovers a tin of letters: her grandfather's correspondence with Julian's father, revealing the deed's 'error' was deliberate—a dying man's scheme to reunite them. Rosalind, feeling managed and betrayed, withdraws and decides to sell at the end-of-summer auction. The beat: the climax's wound—love discovered inside a manipulation.

chapters.title: Bid With the Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the auction, Rosalind plans to sell until Julian publicly reads one of her grandfather's letters—and her own pen name, claiming her novels taught him to come back. She outbids the developer with her book advance, and they sign the deed as partners, then something less legalistic. The beat: the whole heart, risked and kept.
